# University Courses in Audit Mode

_8 offer(s). Part of The Actually-Free Job Training Directory; go [back to the index](../index.md)._

Real university course material you can read, watch, and work through without paying. In almost every case the catch is the same: no graded feedback and no certificate. You trade the paper for the knowledge.

| Offer | Provider | What free means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [MIT OpenCourseWare](#entry-mit-ocw) | Massachusetts Institute of Technology | 100% free |
| [MIT Open Learning Library](#entry-mit-oll) | Massachusetts Institute of Technology | 100% free |
| [Open Yale Courses](#entry-open-yale) | Yale University | 100% free |
| [Open Learning Initiative](#entry-oli-cmu) | Carnegie Mellon University | Self-paced 'independent learner' enrollments are free with a free account |
| [Coursera Audit Mode](#entry-coursera-audit) | Coursera (hosting university content) | The 'Audit' link (visible under the enroll/pay button on supporting courses) opens course content free |
| [edX Audit Track](#entry-edx-audit) | edX (hosting university content) | Choosing 'Audit this course for free' at enrollment gives free content access |
| [OpenLearn](#entry-openlearn) | The Open University (UK) | Free all the way through: courses, and a downloadable Statement of Participation or digital badge for completing many of them |
| [Stanford Online (free courses)](#entry-stanford-online) | Stanford University | Courses marked free are free to enroll and complete |

<a id="entry-mit-ocw"></a>

### MIT OpenCourseWare

**Provider:** Massachusetts Institute of Technology  
**Link:** <https://ocw.mit.edu>

**What it is:** About 2,500 complete MIT courses published openly: lecture videos, notes, assignments, and often exams with solutions. Good for business, math, computer science, and engineering basics.

**What "free" means:** 100% free. No account, no limits, no trial timer. Everything meaningful on the site is free.

**Paper trail:** None. There is no certificate at any price, and no instructor responds to questions.

**Time needed:** A few hours to skim a course; 30-80 study hours for a full one

**Honest catch:** No credit, no credential, no human support. You organize your own learning.

**Tags:** university, no-signup, self-paced, career, tech, stem

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-mit-oll"></a>

### MIT Open Learning Library

**Provider:** Massachusetts Institute of Technology  
**Link:** <https://openlearninglibrary.mit.edu>

**What it is:** A hosted platform version of selected MIT courses with auto-graded exercises, chat-forum-style help threads, and interactive problem sets.

**What "free" means:** 100% free. A free account is required to save progress. No payment step exists.

**Paper trail:** None for most courses. Some issue scans of your work as progress proof, not certificates.

**Time needed:** 10-100 study hours depending on the course

**Honest catch:** Small course list (tens, not thousands). No credit. Certificates generally unavailable even paid.

**Tags:** university, exercises, self-paced, tech

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-open-yale"></a>

### Open Yale Courses

**Provider:** Yale University  
**Link:** <https://oyc.yale.edu>

**What it is:** Full-video recordings of real Yale introductory lectures (financial markets, psychology, game theory, philosophy, economics) with transcripts and reading lists.

**What "free" means:** 100% free. No account needed. Videos and transcripts download readily.

**Paper trail:** None. No certificate, no graded work.

**Time needed:** Whole-semester lecture series, 20-40 hours each

**Honest catch:** Catalog frozen: 'financial markets' etc. recorded years ago, so bits age. Reading lists may point at paid textbooks.

**Tags:** university, lectures, no-signup, business, stem

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-oli-cmu"></a>

### Open Learning Initiative

**Provider:** Carnegie Mellon University  
**Link:** <https://oli.cmu.edu>

**What it is:** Carnegie Mellon's research-built interactive courses (statistics for business, anatomy, biology, logic) with instant-feedback tutoring built in.

**What "free" means:** Self-paced 'independent learner' enrollments are free with a free account. Institutional seats for class use cost money.

**Paper trail:** Progress tracking inside the platform; no formal certificate.

**Time needed:** 20-60 study hours per course

**Honest catch:** Some catalog entries are instructor-only or paid. Confirm the 'self-paced and free' label before committing.

**Tags:** university, exercises, self-paced, business

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-coursera-audit"></a>

### Coursera Audit Mode

**Provider:** Coursera (hosting university content)  
**Link:** <https://www.coursera.org>

**What it is:** Thousands of university and company courses. Audit mode unlocks most video and reading content at no charge.

**What "free" means:** The 'Audit' link (visible under the enroll/pay button on supporting courses) opens course content free. No graded assignments, no certificate.

**Paper trail:** Nothing unless you upgrade to the paid certificate path.

**Time needed:** 3-40 hours per course

**Honest catch:** Not every course supports audit; when audit exists it is easy to miss. Watch for autoplaying free trials of the paid subscription during signup.

**Tags:** university, mooc, self-paced, careful-checkout

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-edx-audit"></a>

### edX Audit Track

**Provider:** edX (hosting university content)  
**Link:** <https://www.edx.org>

**What it is:** Harvard, MIT, and other universities' MOOCs. The audit track is the free version of each supported course.

**What "free" means:** Choosing 'Audit this course for free' at enrollment gives free content access. Graded work, labs, and certificates are behind the paid track.

**Paper trail:** Nothing unless you upgrade to the paid certificate.

**Time needed:** 4-40 hours per course

**Honest catch:** Audit access on some courses expires or lacks later units; many newer programs (MicroMasters, bootcamps) have no audit at all.

**Tags:** university, mooc, self-paced, careful-checkout

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-openlearn"></a>

### OpenLearn

**Provider:** The Open University (UK)  
**Link:** <https://www.open.edu/openlearn>

**What it is:** The Open University's free course collection: hundreds of short, structured units on work skills, business, computing, health, and science.

**What "free" means:** Free all the way through: courses, and a downloadable Statement of Participation or digital badge for completing many of them. Free account required.

**Paper trail:** Free Statement of Participation and/or OpenLearn badge, downloadable as PDF and shareable.

**Time needed:** 3-24 hours per course

**Honest catch:** UK flavor (employment-law and welfare content is UK-specific). Statements are not university credit.

**Tags:** certificate, sign-up, self-paced, career

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08

<a id="entry-stanford-online"></a>

### Stanford Online (free courses)

**Provider:** Stanford University  
**Link:** <https://online.stanford.edu>

**What it is:** Stanford's online course catalog. A running subset of self-paced courses and seminar series are flagged as free to enroll.

**What "free" means:** Courses marked free are free to enroll and complete. Certificate programs and professional courses on the same site are paid.

**Paper trail:** Generally no certificate on the free items; check each course page.

**Time needed:** Varies: 2-60 hours per course

**Honest catch:** You must filter carefully: paid options dominate the catalog and free flags move around.

**Tags:** university, self-paced, career

**Verified free:** 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08
